title: Axis Commerce Operations Guide
readerIntent: Understand how commerce should appear in Nodics Axis without rebuilding separate page-specific functionality.
priorKnowledge: Understand Axis as a BackOffice client over backend-owned contracts.
owner: Axis BackOffice and commerce capability owners
summary: Axis commerce pages should use backend-driven navigation, reusable schema list/detail components, query builder, lifecycle actions, help metadata, documentation links, and consistent selection behavior.

sections.heading: Axis is a client, not a commerce authority
paragraphs: Axis helps business users manage commerce data and operations. It must not own product, price, stock, cart, order, payment, or fulfillment state. It should display and invoke backend-owned contracts through reusable components.

If a page looks similar to Schema Workbench, that is acceptable only when it adds business grouping, help, documentation, safe defaults, and action context. It should not duplicate CRUD logic or create a second implementation path.

sections.heading: Reusable UI patterns
items: Navigation groups and pages come from backend BackOffice metadata.
List/grid components support backend-driven columns, order, sorting, export, pagination, vertical scroll, horizontal scroll, and configurable visibility.
Search and advanced query use the shared query builder where schema data is listed.
Selecting a row opens the reusable schema detail panel under the list, not a page-specific view pattern.
Referenced schema values are clickable and can open related detail while keeping the current row context visible.
Media fields use reusable media preview/detail components where applicable.
Each page heading can show reusable info and documentation icons backed by framework documentation links.
Lifecycle actions are displayed from backend metadata and only enabled when permission and backend operation support exist.

sections.heading: Commerce navigation expectation
items: Catalog: catalogs, catalog versions, categories, products, variants, units, keywords, classification, publishing, and enrichment.
Commerce Operations: stores, warehouses, stock, carts, orders, payment, fulfillment, delivery, returns, operational failures, audit, and reconciliation.
Future sections can add promotions, coupons, tax, fraud, notification, customer service, subscription, marketplace, and analytics when backend capabilities exist.

sections.heading: Page behavior expectation
items: A Products page should show product-specific list, search, create/update where authorized, product detail, media references, price/stock references, and documentation links.
A Stock page should show balances, reservations, allocations, movements, sourcing, reconciliation, and operational actions grouped by business meaning.
A Payment page should show methods, providers, transaction evidence, lifecycle actions, retries, and reconciliation with sensitive data hidden.
A Fulfillment page should show modes, providers, consignments, shipments, labels, tracking, returns, lifecycle actions, and reconciliation.
A generic Workbench view remains available for administrators and developers, but business pages should group data by the task the user is trying to complete.

sections.heading: Documentation integration
items: The info icon explains the business meaning in one or two short lines.
The documentation icon opens framework documentation for the selected concept, not only Axis application documentation.
If framework documentation does not exist for a visible concept, that is a documentation gap and should be fixed before the page is considered complete.
Customer modules can add or override documentation links through backend content/component metadata.

sections.heading: Acceptance checklist
items: No page-specific duplicated table/detail/query/media preview logic when a reusable component exists.
No hard-coded help copy or documentation URLs in Axis when backend metadata can provide them.
No action button without backend-owned lifecycle metadata and permission checks.
Consistent spacing, header background, hover color, sorting, export, grid settings, pagination, and selected-row behavior across commerce pages.
Schema-driven field additions from customer modules can appear in lists/details through backend metadata.
